item: A fetched page is decoded in the encoding its bytes are in: valid UTF-8 first, then the header, then the page's own meta charset (R699 cause 2, Lane V)
summary: The 2026-10-06 triage found Chinese keywords like еӣҫе: UTF-8 read as ptcp154. Measured: charset_normalizer answers ptcp154 for a UTF-8 Chinese page with one stray byte or a body cut mid-character, and the fetcher asked it whenever a server named no charset; it never read the page's meta charset. Order now: byte-order mark, a declared UTF-16/32, the bytes being UTF-8 (at most one invalid sequence per 50 valid non-ASCII characters, one allowed from 8, a cut final character ignored; this overrides a declared single-byte charset), a declared charset other than requests' default ISO-8859-1, the meta declaration in the first 4 KB, the guesser, UTF-8. Every answer is a codec Python knows. New articles only; existing articles keep their stored text (a re-fetch is the only fix for an already-garbled body).
